editorial.description_en: Bisque-fired clay with no glaze on it. The strongest clay colour at this lightness, and the one most people would recognise as terracotta.
editorial.description_ja: 釉薬をかけずに焼いた器のような、赤い土の色。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.688, C 0.092, h 52.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 素 (su, plain) + 焼き (yaki, firing) — the ordinary term for bisque, used here as a colour name. It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Unglazed Ware" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 素焼. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — aka-tsuchi at ΔE00 3.9, tsuchi-gawara at ΔE00 7.1, kari-ato at ΔE00 10.3. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (232°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
